**What type of PR is this?**
> Uncomment only one ` /kind <>` line, hit enter to put that in a new line, and remove leading whitespaces from that line:
>

/kind bug


**What this PR does / why we need it**:
When kubelet is restarted, it will now remove the resources for huge
page sizes no longer supported. This is required when:
- node disables huge pages
- changing the default huge page size in older versions of linux
(because it will then only support the newly set default).
- Software updates that change what sizes are supported (eg. by changing
boot parameters).

In the same way as other resource types, we should also do a cleanup when given resources are no longer supported. The scheduler will handle this without a problem. There should be no backwards compatibility issues, since this would previously result in a crash in kubelet.

Hi,

Ref. the error message, it looks like you have allocated hugepages for multiple sizes, `may not have pre-allocated hugepages for multiple page sizes`.

Can you run: `cat /sys/kernel/mm/hugepages/hugepages-*/nr_hugepages` to verify? If more than one of the numbers is `> 0`, that is the reason. @DeepLJH0001 

This is currently being discussed in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/77251, and the reason for implementing the check is here: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/837/files#r133337110.

Imo. this should be supported, and it would only require removing an if statement in order to implement it. I see no reason to limit the node from allocating huge pages with more than one size.

Because of how it is implemented, adding support for allowing a pod to request huge pages with multiple sizes isn't trivial, and will require some potentially breaking changes, but that is not relevant to this problem. 😄

/cc @mattjmcnaughton @derekwaynecarr
Also, can you also provide the result of `ls /sys/kernel/mm/hugepages`, that will list the supported huge page sizes (both when `default_hugepagesz=1GB` is set, and when it is not.).

Thanks @DeepLJH0001 !

Looks like your kernel only enables huge pages with the default size. My kernel 5.0+ enable all (atleast 2MiB and 1GiB on x86_64) by default.

When the node booted with default_hugepagesz=1GB it "removed support" the 2MiB one, and becuse kubelet use patch on the node status when connecting to the api server, you ended up with both `hugepages-1Gi` and `hugepages-2Mi`, even tho 2Mi wast supported by your machine (the sw, not the hw). Even if the `may not have pre-allocated hugepages for multiple page sizes` error is removed, this will result in a crash when kubelet tries to write to the 2MiB hugetlb cgroup files.

I think using `default_hugepagesz=1G hugepagesz=1G hugepages=32 hugepagesz=2M hugepages=0` should work, otherwise the only current solution is to remove the node from the cluster, and rejoin afterwords.

Ref. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/80576 it looks like you have sorted out the problem, but I still think this is a valid issue, so don't close it.


The correct behaviour for kubelet is to remove unsupported sizes, and only allow use of the supported ones.

"Imo. this should be supported, and it would only require removing an if statement in order to implement it. I see no reason to limit the node from allocating huge pages with more than one size."

Could you fix this one as well?
We use 2M pages only for pods but we need 1G pages for system processes.
So it was little surprising when k8s doesn't start because two different pages were configured no matter they are really used or not.
Thanks!

review_comments: I'd suggest to use ```systemctl stop``` here. Unlike ```systemctl kill``` it will use official configured way to stop the service. If killing kubelet is mandatory for your tests then it would be better to call this function killKubelet.

When using `systemctl stop` the systemd service will be deleted, making it impossible to start it again.

> If killing kubelet is mandatory for your tests then it would be better to call this function killKubelet.

Not sure what you mean with `killKubelet`.

> When using systemctl stop the systemd service will be deleted, making it impossible to start it again.

Can you elaborate on this? Not sure I follow.

> Not sure what you mean with killKubelet.

I mean that you called function stopKubelet, but it doesn't stop Kubelet, it kills it. I proposed to call it KillKubelet.

> Can you elaborate on this? Not sure I follow.

```bash
# Using stop
> systemd-run --remain-after-exit sleep 100
Running as unit: run-u14192.service
> systemctl stop run-u14192.service
> systemctl start run-u14192.service
Failed to start run-u14192.service: Unit run-u14192.service not found.

# Using kill                                                                                                                                                                                             
> systemd-run --remain-after-exit sleep 100
Running as unit: run-u14224.service 
> systemctl kill run-u14224.service
> systemctl start run-u14224.service
# service is restarted
```

> I mean that you called function stopKubelet, but it doesn't stop Kubelet, it kills it. I proposed to call it KillKubelet.

Aha, I agree that renaming it would make sense. I thought you meant to call a given function named `killKubelet` instead.
we can rename the function in a follow-on, but i don't see a major reason to block on the core issue addressed in the pr.

I need to catch-up on latest state of this code, but we traditionally do not support hot-swap of other resources like cpu or memory for a same named node without a restart.  i thought i had seen a similar pr with an update in this space last year, and so I need to refresh my own memory if we handled hugepages separately.
well, devices would get updated as a counted resource.

Well, currently kubelet will report the new kubelet will report updated node resources once in a while (without being restarted), so if you pre-alloc more huge page memory, it will be updated on the fly. This fix only ensures that huge page sizes no longer supported on the node are removed. Today that dosen't happen, and the resource will just stay.

Also, this code is only executed on startup of kubelet, so it will run on both a kubelet restart and a node reboot.
this is a rare test that we can exercise with hugepages in shared testing infrastructure as it does not depend on native support in the test environment.

Hmm. This test require a restart of the kubelet (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/80831/files#diff-c50317a607de218aa9893a10fb6e0fb1R223), so I think we need to keep it a serial node e2e test, or?

> @bart0sh where this function is used and how is it related to this PR?

It is used here
Can you explain why stopKubelet function returns another function that starts Kubelet? It doesn't look very clear and logical to me to be honest.

If you look at the func it make more sense. We have to store the name of the service somewhere, and imo. it is cleaner to use a closure like this instead of returning the name, or even storing it in a var.

If you have a better idea ill be happy to change the behavior! :)

I'd say storing it in var is much more clear, readable and allows to check if the action succeeded:
```
kubeletServiceName := findRunningKubletServiceName()
err := killKubelet(kubeletServiceName)
...
err := startKubelet(kubeletServiceName)
```

I guess we can do that, but then we will have to check with the folks from `sig-testing`. 

Doing that will move the logic for handling the different background services into the test, making it hard to refactor the code later. In case we start supporting other ways to run kubelet in the tests than `systemd`, we will have to change the tests too, not just the utilities.

I do think I prefer to separate the two concerns, but ill defer the decision to `sig-testing`.

cc @oomichi

I think either me or you misunderstood something. I'm not proposing to support other ways to run kubelet. My proposal is to get rid of closure.
Here is how killKubelet functions would look like:

```
func killKubelet(kubeletServiceName string) error {
	stdout, err := exec.Command("sudo", "systemctl", "kill", kubeletServiceName).CombinedOutput()
        framework.ExpectNoError(err, "Failed to kill kubelet with systemctl: %v, %v", err, stdout)
        return err
}

```

> I'm not proposing to support other ways to run kubelet. My proposal is to get rid of closure.

Adding this code to the test will imo. move the logic of handlig the liveness of kubelet into the test, instead of a central & reusable place.
```go
kubeletServiceName := findRunningKubletServiceName()
err := killKubelet(kubeletServiceName)
...
err := startKubelet(kubeletServiceName)
````

I do agree that `no closure  > closure`, but I am not that happy with moving the systemd-logic into the test. But again, ill defer to sig-testing.

Long term the best solution would be to expose these `cmd`s into the `e2e_node/utils`, but that is outside the scope of this PR.
